MODULE 1: FULL OUTLINE

TIP-OFF

Basketball School

## TIP-OFF

is our opening huddle where coaches welcome the players as a group and set the expectations for the day. The Tip-Off should take no longer than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are 5 parts that should be covered in every Tip-Off:

### CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

### CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

### COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

### COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

### CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together! "NBA Basketball School on 3! (Location Name) on 6!"

PARTNER TAG GAME

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no basket needed)

#### EQUIPMENT

None needed. Can add 1 ball per player for dribbling loads.

#### DESCRIPTION

Give players 10 seconds to find a partner. On "go," both players attempt to tag their partner's knees simultaneously. Play tag for 30 to 60 seconds. Each player should keep track of how many tags they get. Change partners after two loads have been applied to tag games.

#### SCORING

Players get 1 point for tag.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Scanning and reading the playing area
- Creativity
- Changing speed and direction
- Deking and juking

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- While moving, tag partner's back.
- While crawling, tag partner's back.
- While hopping on one leg, tag partner's hips.
- While jumping on two legs, tag partner's hips.
- While dribbling, tag partner's knees.
- While dribbling, only use weak hand to tag partner's hips.
- While dribbling, steal their partner's ball.
- While dribbling, each player must keep one foot on part of any line within the gym while still trying to steal their partner's ball. Both feet off the line leads to a point for the partner.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage players to find a way to tag your opponent, while avoiding being tagged.
- Ensure players change partners after every two rounds.
- Watch for kids who have their head down and encourage them to keep eyes up.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

?

- "What are the best ways to fake someone out?"
- "Why is changing speeds important?"

WARM-UP

Basketball School

4-ON-2 PASSING RONDO

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no basket needed). Mark out squares using 4 cones with every cone approximately 6 steps away.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball and 4 cones per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Four players will act as passers, who cannot move and must stand over the cones. Two defenders stand in the middle. The passers have to keep the ball away from the defenders. A defender switches with a passer if they tag the player with the ball, deflect a pass, or steal a ball. This game can also be played 4-on-3, 5-on-2, 5-on-3, etc. subject to group numbers and space. Each load can be played for 2 to 3 minutes.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Say the name of the teammate you pass to.
- Can only take one dribble.
- Can only pass with one hand.
- After making a pass, exchange spots with a teammate.
- Continually move around in the space (e.g. 4-on-2 keepaway).

#### SCORING

Not needed due to warm-up. Players get 1 point for every completed pass (if desired).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Mark out squares with cones quickly and efficiently so players do not waste time waiting.
- Ensure players switch roles so players experience both offense and defense.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Identifying the open player
- Faking a pass then making a pass
- Changing angle of pass

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where was the open player?"
- "What can you do to be surprising on defense?"

GAME TIME

## GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.
